title: Learning the Body
logline: Young novices learn to recite the body's thirty-two parts aloud, forwards and then backwards, stumbling over the reverse order until a teacher corrects them.

object.note: Object 7 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: Sight restored becomes the body named part by part: young novices reciting its thirty-two parts, an echo of the novices in 'Learning the Map' who memorised the mind.

thread_out.thread: The body recited from the outside becomes a body built out of sight: a midwife's rounds following pregnancies week by week.

lesson.in_simple_terms: Saying the body's ordinary parts aloud, one by one, forwards and backwards, slowly turns 'my body' from one smooth whole into a list of things. The texts give this as a first lesson to new novices.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: ශරීරයේ සාමාන්‍ය කොටස් එකින් එක, ඉදිරියටත් ආපසුත් හඬ නගා කීමෙන්, 'මගේ ශරීරය' ලෙස එක් මුළු දෙයක් සේ පෙනුණු දේ ක්‍රමයෙන් කොටස් ලැයිස්තුවක් බවට පත් වන බව මෙයින් පෙනේ.
lesson.the_teaching: Mindfulness of the body, as the Margaya teaches it, works with the body's thirty-two parts, from head hair to brain, and it names this as the first meditation subject given to those newly ordained. The parts are learned in small groups, recited aloud for days forwards and backwards, and the student moves on only once the words begin to call up the parts themselves; in the end all thirty-two are recited together in both directions. The Pradeepika compares the names to a palm-leaf marker tied on the way to a forest well: needed at first, dropped once the path is worn. The same Margaya tells students to learn the twenty-eight kinds of matter by heart, so counting a whole into its parts is itself a way of attending.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: The film stays with the daily recitation: small voices chanting a fixed list, faltering on the reverse order, a teacher stepping in to correct a skipped part, while sweeping, meals and washing robes go on around the lesson. Moments when a novice glances at a hand or at skin while saying a word let the viewer feel the list touching a real body, without anyone explaining what the practice is for.

key_terms.en: recitation, verbal and then mental rehearsal

lesson.caution: This is neither 'hate your body' nor 'love your body': the texts ask for letting go of both craving and aversion, and their traditional descriptions of the body's parts are not anatomy or medical fact.
lesson.builds_on: After a film about a sense held as most truly 'mine', this one shows a practice that loosens that grip by naming the body part by part, out loud.
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
